g.text: MEDIT · Drivers — its clients; Modbench is the right column, its client the seam
MODBENCH · Drivers — the user, in VS Code's trees, panels and palette
MEDIT · Driving adapters — the API and the watcher
MODBENCH · Driving adapters — the views: read a value, fire a command
MEDIT · Core — the write side and the read side; each references Access and the kernel
MODBENCH · Core — one command per gesture, beside the codec of the file it writes; each writes through MO2 files and forgets
MEDIT · Kernel — read by Core and Access; a port lives here; a kernel box references only Vocabulary
One arrow per reference, from the box that references to the box it references.

A box's reference list is the arrows that leave it here, plus its column's kernel by the band's rule. Every arrow points down or into the kernel; a port lives in the kernel, so the box that implements it and the boxes that call it both reference the kernel. A composition root, the HTTP endpoints on mEdit and Toolbox and the activation file on Modbench, references every box below it by definition. A reference this picture does not draw is a question for the maintainer, never a line an agent adds.
MODBENCH · Kernel — pure; read by Core and Access, the record panel included; a port lives here; a kernel box references nothing
MEDIT · Driven adapters — the record index is a view over the two beside it
MODBENCH · Driven adapters — MO2 files is the one reader and writer of the instance; the Instance is derived from it by watching, and nothing else
MODBENCH · Systems of record; mEdit is the left column and always running
